sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Crestview different from South Florida?
sections.html:
Crestview is an Okaloosa County city, and its owner-occupied homes are valued modestly. Census prices the typical owned home at $277,900 for 2020-2024, below the $332,700 national figure in the same series.

Growth is the local story. Headcounts climbed from 20,978 in 2010 to 27,134 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 31,193 is 13.8 percent above the 2020 estimates base. Household income in the middle of the pack is $65,480, which shapes what local buyers can pay.

sections.h2: What does Crestview housing look like in the Census data?
sections.html:
The city spreads over 16.58 square miles and in 2020 it held roughly 1,636.8 people for each square mile. Owners live in 61.3 percent of its homes.

sections.h2: Who lives in Crestview and where do they work?
sections.html:
The population skews young: 28.3 percent are under 18, 8.0 percent are under 5, and 11.2 percent are 65 or older.

  • Civilian labor force participation sits at 57.4 percent for ages 16 and up.
  • The commute averages 30.4 minutes against 26.4 nationally.
  • Local retail sales totaled $931,900 thousand in 2022, and health care receipts were $308,563 thousand.

Census puts bachelor's attainment at 22.6 percent, while 92.1 percent finished high school.

sections.h2: Which Okaloosa County offices handle a Crestview sale?
sections.html:
Three Okaloosa County offices matter: the property appraiser (values), the tax collector (bills) and the circuit court clerk (deed recording). Each is one of five elected county posts that also include the sheriff and the supervisor of elections.

The appraiser sets January 1 values and rules on exemptions. The collector handles bills, deferrals, installments and certificate sales, and the clerk takes deed tax at recording. Ask each office for forms, hours and current fees on your parcel.

sections.h2: What taxes apply when a Crestview home is sold?
sections.html:
Okaloosa falls under the standard 70 cents per $100 deed rate on the Revenue Department's page, and the rate is written into s. 201.02. All parties on the document are liable whichever one agrees to pay.

  • Filing a deed costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per further page, plus add-on charges.
  • Each name beyond four adds $1.00.
  • Two witnesses must sign the deed.

Quitclaim deeds are taxable too. A spousal transfer of a homestead where the only consideration is a mortgage may be exempt.

sections.h2: How do homestead rules affect Crestview sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
Homestead lowers a Crestview owner's taxable value by up to $50,000, with $25,000 of it reaching school taxes. It ends on sale, on renting out the house, or when the house stops being the permanent home.

The Save Our Homes cap is the smaller of 3 percent or CPI. With the city adding people quickly, market values may outrun it, so a buyer's first bill can jump. Property without homestead has a 10 percent yearly limit. Any sale or foreclosure resets just value the next January 1.

sections.h2: What if a Crestview house is tenant-occupied, inherited or behind on payments?
sections.html:
Florida attaches fixed steps to each case.

  • Tenants: 3 days for unpaid rent, 7 days on lease violations, 30 days to end a monthly tenancy.
  • Estates: shortened administration at $150,000 or less, and creditors have three months after first notice.
  • Foreclosure: auction within 20 to 35 days, 5 percent deposit, 10 days to object.

People with no lease are treated differently. An owner may file a sworn sheriff complaint to remove them, though a false statement risks damages of triple the fair market rent.

sections.h2: What does the Florida tax calendar look like for a Crestview owner?
sections.html:
Okaloosa County follows the statewide yearly pattern.

  • January 1: the assessment date.
  • March 1: exemption filing closes.
  • August: proposed-tax notices go out.
  • 25 days after that notice: last day to petition on value.
  • November: bills arrive; early payment earns 4 percent off in November, falling to 1 percent by February.
  • April 1: late.

Ask your closing agent how the yearly bill will be split.

sections.h2: What happens if Crestview property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid accounts are sold as certificates by June 1 to whoever bids the lowest interest. The holder must wait two years from April 1 of the issue year before pressing the owner or applying for a deed, and the application costs $75.

For a homestead, the opening bid at a tax deed sale adds half the assessed value to what is owed. The winning bidder pays a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is more. Selling and paying at closing resolves things sooner.

sections.h2: Can a Crestview owner use a life estate deed or transfer to family?
sections.html:
Moving title to relatives usually counts as a change of ownership unless an exception such as a spousal transfer applies. The Revenue Department also lists quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed as taxable.

A so-called lady bird deed was addressed in a 2020 Department of Revenue advisement, which said that the deed on the facts presented transfers no present beneficial interest and so carries no doc stamp tax. That advisement turned on its facts, so have a Florida attorney review any such deed before relying on it.

sections.h2: How does Crestview compare with national figures?
sections.html:
On the same 2020-2024 Census series, Crestview home values and incomes both run below the national numbers.

  • Typical rent: $1,366 here against $1,413 nationally.
  • Typical household income: $65,480 against $80,734.
  • Poverty rate: 11.2 percent against 10.2 percent.
  • Residents under 65 without health insurance: 12.7 percent against 9.6 percent.

Per capita income in the city is $31,018, and retail sales per person were $32,958 in 2022. A buyer here is often watching the monthly payment closely, which makes a clear estimate of taxes and insurance useful when you negotiate.

sections.h2: What does the community look like beyond housing?
sections.html:
Census describes a city with 60.5 percent White alone, 20.4 percent Black alone, 3.0 percent Asian alone and 10.8 percent Hispanic or Latino residents. Foreign-born residents are 5.1 percent, and 9.3 percent of residents aged five and over speak another language at home.

Few people move within a year: 80.0 percent stayed put. Computers are in 96.7 percent of households and broadband in 93.0 percent, so online listings and electronic document signing are practical here. Persons with a disability under 65 are 12.4 percent of that age group, which matters when a seller or buyer asks about accessible features.

sections.h2: What should a Crestview seller line up before listing?
sections.html:
• A payoff figure from your lender and a list of any liens on the parcel.
  • The current homestead status, since an exemption you hold ends when the house changes hands.
  • Receipts for any permits, so a buyer's lender does not stall on them. Contact the City of Crestview for permit history at your address.
  • A plan for the deed: two witnesses, recording at the Okaloosa clerk, and the stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 shared among the parties.
  • A written answer from the tax collector on whether a deferral or installment plan exists on your account.

With a younger-than-average population and an average commute of 30.4 minutes, a tidy file of records makes it easier for a buyer to commit.

faqs.q: What does a Crestview home typically cost?

faqs.a: Fast. The July 2025 estimate of 31,193 is 13.8 percent above the 2020 base.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Crestview?
faqs.a: Yes, the deed tax is 70 cents per $100 and all parties are liable. The sales contract decides who pays.

faqs.q: Who can tell me my current property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Okaloosa tax collector bills each November, and the appraiser explains the value behind it.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell a house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually not until the personal representative has authority. Ask a probate lawyer or the clerk about the right track, such as summary administration for smaller estates.
